subject: math
title: Grade 8 Angle Properties: Parallel Lines, Transversals and Polygons
seo_title: Grade 8 Angle Properties Worksheets: Parallel Lines and Polygons, Free Math with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Solve problems involving angle properties, including the properties of intersecting and parallel lines and of polygons
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets on angle properties for the Ontario curriculum: supplementary and complementary angles, vertically opposite angles, corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles on parallel lines, triangles and quadrilaterals, and interior angles of polygons with (n − 2) × 180°. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: On parallel lines, corresponding and alternate angles are equal, and co-interior angles add up to 180°.
key_sub: Supplementary angles add up to 180° and complementary angles to 90°. Vertically opposite angles are equal. A triangle’s angles add up to 180°, a quadrilateral’s to 360°, and any polygon’s to (n − 2) × 180°.
body_html:
Pairs of angles

Supplementary angles add up to 180°, like angles on a straight line. Complementary angles add up to 90°, like the two parts of a right angle. When two lines cross, the vertically opposite angles are equal.

Supplement and complement

Find the supplement and the complement of 38°.

Supplement: 180° − 38° = 142°. Complement: 90° − 38° = 52°.

Answer: 142° and 52°

Parallel lines and a transversal

A transversal is a line that crosses two other lines. Arrows on the lines show they are parallel. Then three pairs of angles follow a rule.

PairWhere they areRule
CorrespondingSame position at each crossing pointEqual
AlternateBetween the lines, opposite sides of the transversalEqual
Co-interiorBetween the lines, same side of the transversalAdd up to 180°
Use algebra

Two co-interior angles are 2x and x + 30°. Find x.

Co-interior angles add up to 180°: 3x + 30° = 180°. 3x = 150°, so x = 50°.

Answer: x = 50°

Triangles, quadrilaterals and polygons

The angles in a triangle add up to 180°. The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior angles that are not next to it. A polygon with n sides splits into n − 2 triangles from one vertex, so its interior angles add up to (n − 2) × 180°.

PolygonSidesSum of interior anglesEach angle if regular
Triangle31 × 180° = 180°60°
Quadrilateral42 × 180° = 360°90°
Pentagon53 × 180° = 540°108°
Hexagon64 × 180° = 720°120°
Octagon86 × 180° = 1080°135°
Regular octagon

A stop sign is a regular octagon. Find each interior angle.

Sum: (8 − 2) × 180° = 1080°. The 8 angles are equal: 1080° ÷ 8 = 135°.

Answer: 135°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up alternate and co-interior anglesZ shape: equal. C shape (same side, between the lines): add up to 180°
Using 360° for the angles in a triangleA triangle is 180°. A quadrilateral is 360°
Mixing up supplementary and complementarySupplementary: 180°. Complementary: 90°
Using n × 180° for a polygonUse (n − 2) × 180°: a hexagon is 4 × 180° = 720°
Using the angle rules when the lines are not parallelLook for the arrows. Without them, corresponding angles need not be equal

faq.q: What angle properties do Grade 8 students learn in Ontario?
faq.a: In Spatial Sense (E2.2), they solve problems with the angle properties of intersecting lines, parallel lines cut by a transversal (corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles) and polygons, including the sum of interior angles, (n − 2) × 180°.

faq.q: What is the difference between alternate and co-interior angles?
faq.a: Both pairs are between the parallel lines. Alternate angles are on opposite sides of the transversal (a Z shape) and are equal; co-interior angles are on the same side (a C shape) and add up to 180°.

faq.q: How do you find the sum of the interior angles of a polygon?
faq.a: Use (n − 2) × 180°, where n is the number of sides. A hexagon has (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°, so each angle of a regular hexagon is 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.

faq.q: What is the difference between supplementary and complementary angles?
faq.a: Supplementary angles add up to 180°, like angles on a straight line. Complementary angles add up to 90°, like the two parts of a right angle.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The three angles make a straight line: 180°. 38° + 57° = 95°, and 180° − 95° = 85°. (95° is the sum of the known angles, not the missing one.)

items.q: What is the complement of 34°?
items.e: Complementary angles add up to 90°. 90° − 34° = 56°. (146° is the supplement: 180° − 34°.)

items.q: The whole angle is a right angle. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The two angles are complementary: they add up to 90°. 90° − 37° = 53°. (143° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: Angles A and B are supplementary. Angle A = 3x and angle B = x + 40°. What is the value of x?
An angle and its complement differ by 18°. What is the larger angle?
items.e: The two angles add up to 90°. 90° − 18° = 72°, and 72° ÷ 2 = 36° is the smaller angle. The larger is 36° + 18° = 54°. (99° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: An angle is 5 times as big as its supplement. How big is the angle?
items.e: The angle is 5 parts and its supplement is 1 part: 6 parts = 180°, so 1 part = 30°. The angle is 5 × 30° = 150°. (30° is the supplement.)
The line is tilted, but it is still straight, so the angles add up to 180°. 180° − 65° = 115°.

items.q: The whole angle is a right angle. What is the value of x?
Which pair of angles is complementary?
items.e: Complementary angles add up to 90°: 27° + 63° = 90°. 27° and 153° (and 63° and 117°) add up to 180°, so they are supplementary.

items.q: The whole angle is a right angle. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The two angles are complementary: they add up to 90°. 90° − 64° = 26°. (116° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: What is the supplement of 112°?
items.e: Supplementary angles add up to 180°. 180° − 112° = 68°. (22° comes from 112° − 90°, and 248° from 360° − 112°.)
Angles on a straight line are supplementary: they add up to 180°. 180° − 48° = 132°. (42° comes from using 90°, the rule for complementary angles.)

items.q: Can an obtuse angle have a complement?
c: Only if it is less than 180°
No, it is already more than 90°
items.e: Complementary angles add up to 90°. An obtuse angle is more than 90° on its own, so no angle can be added to it to make 90°.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. What is the value of x?
items.e: x + x + 3x = 5x = 180°, so x = 180° ÷ 5 = 36°. Check: 36° + 36° + 108° = 180°. (60° comes from dividing by 3, the number of angles, not by 5.)

items.q: Two angles are complementary. One is 4 times the other. What is the smaller angle?
items.e: The angles are 1 part and 4 parts: 5 parts = 90°, so 1 part = 18°. The angles are 18° and 72°. (36° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: Which pair of angles is supplementary?
items.e: Supplementary angles add up to 180°: 104° + 76° = 180°. 14° + 76° = 90° (complementary), 104° + 86° = 190° and 76° + 284° = 360°.

items.q: Arjun says the complement of 40° is 140°. Is he right?
items.e: Complementary angles add up to 90°, so the complement is 90° − 40° = 50°. 140° is the supplement (180° − 40°).

items.q: Two angles are supplementary. One is 30° more than the other. What is the larger angle?
items.e: Take away the extra 30°: 180° − 30° = 150°, and 150° ÷ 2 = 75° for the smaller angle. The larger angle is 75° + 30° = 105°. Check: 75° + 105° = 180°.

items.q: What is the supplement of the complement of 25°?
items.e: First the complement: 90° − 25° = 65°. Then its supplement: 180° − 65° = 115°. (155° is the supplement of 25° itself.)

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 40° angle, so the two are equal: 40°.

The two angles are next to each other on a straight line, so 3x + x + 20° = 180°. 4x = 160°, so x = 40°. Check: 120° + 60° = 180°. (10° comes from making them equal, but only vertically opposite angles are equal.)

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 65° angle, so the two are equal: 65°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. One of the angles is 47°. What do the two obtuse angles add up to?
items.e: Each obtuse angle is next to a 47° angle: 180° − 47° = 133°. The two obtuse angles are equal: 133° + 133° = 266°. Check: 47° + 47° + 266° = 360°.
The missing angle is vertically opposite the 145° angle, so the two are equal: 145°.
Vertically opposite angles are across the crossing point from each other: a and c (also b and d). Angles next to each other, like a and b, are supplementary.
The missing angle and 58° are next to each other on a straight line, so they are supplementary: 180° − 58° = 122°. (58° would be the vertically opposite angle.)
a is on a straight line with 64°: 180° − 64° = 116°. b is vertically opposite 64°, so b = 64°. c is vertically opposite a, so c = 116°.
The missing angle and 130° are next to each other on a straight line, so they are supplementary: 180° − 130° = 50°. (130° would be the vertically opposite angle.)

items.q: Hana says that vertically opposite angles are supplementary. Is she right?
c: Yes, they are on a straight line
items.e: Vertically opposite angles are equal. The angles next to each other (on a straight line) are the supplementary ones.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. What is the value of x?
items.e: Vertically opposite angles are equal: 2x + 10° = 70°. 2x = 60°, so x = 30°. (40° comes from adding 10° instead of subtracting it.)

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Two vertically opposite angles add up to 100°. How big is each of the other two angles?
items.e: The two equal opposite angles are 100° ÷ 2 = 50° each. The angles next to them are 180° − 50° = 130°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 72° angle, so the two are equal: 72°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. What is the value of x?
items.e: Vertically opposite angles are equal: 4x − 20° = 2x + 30°. Take 2x from both sides: 2x − 20° = 30°. 2x = 50°, so x = 25°. Check: 4 × 25° − 20° = 80° and 2 × 25° + 30° = 80°. (80° is the angle, not x.)

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Find the missing angle.
items.e: 35° + 85° + the angle above them make a straight line: 180° − 120° = 60°. The missing angle is vertically opposite that angle, so it is 60° too.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 80° angle, so it is also 80°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The three angles are on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 50° + 60° = 110°, and 180° − 110° = 70°.

items.q: What is true about vertically opposite angles?
items.e: When two straight lines cross, the angles opposite each other are equal. Angles next to each other add up to 180°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. One angle is 4 times the angle next to it. What is the smaller angle?
items.e: Angles next to each other add up to 180°. 1 part + 4 parts = 5 parts = 180°, so the smaller angle is 36°. (72° comes from sharing 360° instead of 180°.)

items.q: Two straight lines cross. One of the angles is a right angle. What are the other three angles?
items.e: The angle next to 90° is 180° − 90° = 90°, and opposite angles are equal. So all four angles are 90°: the lines are perpendicular.

sets.title: Parallel lines: corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles

items.q: The arrows show that the two lines are parallel. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The angles are between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal. Alternate angles are equal: 70°.
The angles are between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal (a Z shape). They are alternate angles, so they are equal: 125°. (55° would be co-interior angles.)

items.q: The arrows show that the two lines are parallel. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The angles are between the parallel lines, on the same side of the transversal. Co-interior angles add up to 180°: 180° − 125° = 55°.
The angles are corresponding, so they are equal: 3x = 105°, and x = 105° ÷ 3 = 35°. (25° comes from 3x = 75°, as if they added up to 180°.)

items.q: Mei says that alternate angles on parallel lines add up to 180°. Is she right?
c: Yes, they are between the lines
Yes, they make a Z shape
items.e: Alternate angles (Z shape) are equal. Co-interior angles (C shape) are the ones that add up to 180°.

items.q: The arrows show that the two lines are parallel. What kind of angles are a and b?
items.e: They are between the parallel lines, on the same side of the transversal (a C shape): co-interior angles. They add up to 180°.

items.q: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, co-interior angles …
items.e: Co-interior angles are between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal. They add up to 180°.

items.q: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, corresponding angles are …
items.e: Corresponding angles sit in the same position at each crossing point, so they are equal. Co-interior angles are the ones that are supplementary.
They are in the same position at each crossing point (an F shape): corresponding angles. They are equal.

items.q: The arrows show that the two lines are parallel. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The two angles are in the same position at each crossing point, so they are corresponding angles. Corresponding angles are equal: 70°.

items.q: The arrows show that the two lines are parallel. What is the value of x?
items.e: The angles are co-interior, so they add up to 180°: 2x + x + 30° = 180°. 3x = 150°, so x = 50°. Check: 100° + 80° = 180°. (30° comes from making them equal, as if they were alternate.)
They are between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal (a Z shape): alternate angles. They are equal.

items.q: A transversal crosses two lines. Two corresponding angles are both 64°. Are the lines parallel?
c: No, they must add up to 90°
No, they must add up to 180°
items.e: When corresponding angles are equal, the lines are parallel. This is how you can check that two lines are parallel.

items.q: The arrows show that the two lines are parallel. Find the missing angle.
items.e: Two steps. The angle in the same place at the lower point is corresponding, so it is 105°. The missing angle is next to it on a straight line: 180° − 105° = 75°.

items.q: The arrows show that the two lines are parallel. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The angles are outside the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal. The angle vertically opposite 48° and the missing angle are corresponding, so the missing angle is 48°.

items.q: The arrows show that the two lines are parallel. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The two angles are in the same position at each crossing point (above the line, right of the transversal). They are corresponding angles, so they are equal: 65°.

items.q: The arrows show that the two lines are parallel. What is the value of x?
items.e: The angles are alternate, so they are equal: 4x − 10° = 70°. 4x = 80°, so x = 20°. (15° comes from subtracting 10° instead of adding it, and 30° from using 180° − 70° = 110°.)

items.q: The arrows show that the two lines are parallel. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The corresponding angle at the lower point is 40°. The missing angle is on a straight line with it: 180° − 40° = 140°.

items.q: The arrows show that the two lines are parallel. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The angles are between the parallel lines, on the same side of the transversal (a C shape). They are co-interior angles, so they add up to 180°: 180° − 120° = 60°. (120° mixes them up with alternate angles.)

items.q: A transversal crosses two lines. Two co-interior angles are 72° and 110°. Are the lines parallel?
c: No, co-interior angles must be equal
items.e: If the lines were parallel, the co-interior angles would add up to exactly 180°. 72° + 110° = 182°, so the lines are not parallel.
The exterior angle 130° equals the sum of the two interior angles that are not next to it: 70° + ? = 130°, so ? = 60°. (50° is the interior angle next to the 130° angle.)

items.q: Which three angles could be the angles of a triangle?
items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 50° + 60° + 70° = 180°. The others add up to 190°, 200° and 360°.
The left side crosses the two parallel sides, so the angles at its ends are co-interior: they add up to 180°. 180° − 64° = 116°. (64° would only be right for alternate angles.)

items.q: Find the missing angle in this triangle.
items.e: The small square is a right angle (90°). The other two angles add up to 180° − 90° = 90°, so 90° − 38° = 52°.
The angles in a triangle add up to 180°. 63° + 45° = 108°, and 180° − 108° = 72°. (252° comes from using 360°.)

items.q: This is an isosceles triangle. The marks show the two equal sides. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The two base angles are equal, so both are 67°. 67° + 67° = 134°, and 180° − 134° = 46°. (113° comes from 180° − 67°, forgetting the second base angle.)
The angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360°. 80° + 115° + 70° = 265°, and 360° − 265° = 95°.

items.q: This is a kite. Its two side angles are equal. Find the missing angle.

items.e: The angles in a triangle add up to 180°. 50° + 60° = 110°, and 180° − 110° = 70°. (250° comes from using 360°.)
The angles in a triangle add up to 180°, not 360°. 65° + 45° = 110°, and 180° − 110° = 70°.
The angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360°. 100° + 120° + 75° = 295°, and 360° − 295° = 65°.

items.q: This is an isosceles triangle. The marks show the two equal sides. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The two base angles are equal. 180° − 40° = 140°, and 140° ÷ 2 = 70°. (140° is both base angles together.)

items.q: This is a parallelogram. Find the missing angle.
items.e: The bottom and top sides are parallel, so the angles at the two ends of a slanted side are co-interior: they add up to 180°. 180° − 70° = 110°. Check: 70° + 110° + 70° + 110° = 360°.

items.q: An isosceles triangle has one angle of 100°. What are the other two angles?
items.e: 100° is obtuse, so it must be the angle between the equal sides (two angles of 100° would be more than 180°). 180° − 100° = 80°, and 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.
The two small squares are 90° each. 90° + 90° + 65° = 245°, and 360° − 245° = 115°. (25° comes from using 180°: 180° − 90° − 65°.)

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 37° and 98°. What is the third angle?

items.e: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles that are not next to it: 45° + 60° = 105°. (Or: the interior angle is 180° − 105° = 75°, and 75° + 105° = 180°.)

items.q: The angles of a triangle are x, 2x and 3x. What is the value of x?
The angles of a quadrilateral are x, x, 2x and 2x. What is the value of x?

items.e: The angles in a triangle add up to 180°. 35° + 105° = 140°, and 180° − 140° = 40°. (220° comes from using 360°.)

items.q: This is a regular hexagon. What is the size of each interior angle?
Four interior angles of a pentagon are 100°, 110°, 95° and 120°. What is the fifth angle?
items.e: The sum for a pentagon is (5 − 2) × 180° = 540°. 100° + 110° + 95° + 120° = 425°, and 540° − 425° = 115°. (108° is the angle of a regular pentagon, but this one is not regular.)

items.q: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 140°. How many sides does it have?
items.e: Each exterior angle is 180° − 140° = 40°. The exterior angles add up to 360°: 360° ÷ 40° = 9 sides. Check: (9 − 2) × 180° = 1260°, and 1260° ÷ 9 = 140°.

items.q: The interior angles of a polygon add up to 1260°. How many sides does it have?
items.e: (n − 2) × 180° = 1260°, so n − 2 = 1260 ÷ 180 = 7, and n = 9. (7 forgets to add the 2 back.)

items.q: The loonie, Canada’s $1 coin, has 11 sides. What is the sum of the interior angles of an 11-sided polygon?
A soccer ball is made of regular pentagons and regular hexagons. At each corner, one pentagon and two hexagons meet. What do the three angles at that corner add up to?
items.e: Each pentagon angle is 108° and each hexagon angle is 120°. 108° + 120° + 120° = 348°. That is less than 360°, so the pieces do not lie flat: the ball curves.

items.q: A floor is tiled with regular octagons and squares. At each corner, two octagons and one square meet. What do the three angles at that corner add up to?
items.e: Each octagon angle is 135° and each square angle is 90°. 135° + 135° + 90° = 360°, a full turn, so the tiles fit with no gaps.

items.q: Ethan draws lines from one vertex of a stop sign (a regular octagon) to all the other vertices. How many triangles does he make?
items.e: From one vertex you can draw lines to every vertex except itself and its 2 neighbours. An octagon splits into 8 − 2 = 6 triangles.

items.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
The front of an A-frame cabin is an isosceles triangle. The angle at the top is 50°. What angle does each sloping side make with the floor?
items.e: The two base angles are equal. 180° − 50° = 130°, and 130° ÷ 2 = 65°.

items.q: This is a regular pentagon. What is the size of each interior angle?
items.e: Sum: (5 − 2) × 180° = 540°. The 5 angles are equal: 540° ÷ 5 = 108°. (72° is 360° ÷ 5, the exterior angle.)

items.q: A stop sign is a regular octagon. What is the size of each interior angle?
items.e: Sum: (8 − 2) × 180° = 1080°. The 8 angles are equal: 1080° ÷ 8 = 135°. (45° is 360° ÷ 8, the exterior angle.)

items.q: The pentagon is split into triangles from one vertex. What is the sum of its interior angles?
items.e: There are 5 − 2 = 3 triangles, and the angles in each add up to 180°. 3 × 180° = 540°. (900° counts 5 triangles, but there are only 3.)

items.q: Five interior angles of a hexagon are 120°, 115°, 130°, 125° and 110°. What is the sixth angle?
items.e: The sum for a hexagon is (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°. The five angles add up to 600°, and 720° − 600° = 120°. (300° comes from using (6 − 1) × 180° = 900°.)

items.q: The parking lines at a mall are parallel. Each line meets the curb at a 65° angle. What is the angle on the other side of the line, along the same curb?
items.e: The two angles are on a straight line (the curb), so they are supplementary: 180° − 65° = 115°.

items.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a decagon (10 sides)?

Amira leans a ladder against the wall of a cottage to clean the eavestroughs. The wall is vertical and the ground is flat. The ladder makes a 72° angle with the ground. What angle does it make with the wall?
items.e: The wall, the ground and the ladder make a right triangle. 180° − 90° − 72° = 18°. The two acute angles are complementary: 90° − 72° = 18°.

items.q: The interior angles of a hexagon are x, x, x, 2x, 2x and 2x. What is the value of x?
What is the sum of the interior angles of an octagon?
A straight road crosses two parallel railway tracks near Winnipeg. The road makes a 58° angle with the first track. What is the corresponding angle at the second track?
items.e: The tracks are parallel, so corresponding angles are equal: 58°. (122° is the angle on the other side of the road.)
